description: Coverage and test-writing discipline skills: the coverage queue, the report-the-gaps loop, and the test-writer honesty rules.

queries.query: Raise test coverage to 80% on every Go package in this repo that's below it.
Bring every Python module under 75% coverage up to target. Write the tests, then re-measure at the end.
Coverage on our TypeScript packages is all over the place. Queue every file under 70% and write tests until each is at target.
Get the Rust crate's coverage up to 75% per module.
Raise coverage to 90% on every package in this monorepo, Go and Python both. Measure once up front, not between batches.
Measure our current coverage, list the zero-coverage functions and untested packages, then add tests and give me a before/after report.
Raise coverage, then report exactly what's still untested afterwards, prioritized by impact.
Which functions in this repo have zero test coverage? Write tests for the most important ones and show me the delta.
Before you write any tests, measure baseline coverage and tell me where the biggest gaps are, then fix the worst ones.
Write tests for the payments package, and don't touch or rewrite any of the existing tests.
Last time an agent overwrote my test files and claimed coverage improved without measuring. Add tests to internal/queue and report from git diff.
Extend the existing test suite for the parser, and make sure your report lists only the files you actually changed.
Add tests for src/auth and report the real build and test exit codes, not a summary.
Write unit tests for the new retry helper in pkg/retry without changing the code under test.
What's a good code coverage target for a CLI tool?
Explain the difference between statement coverage and branch coverage.
Set up Codecov uploads in our GitHub Actions workflow.
TestServerShutdown fails about one run in ten. Find out why.
Delete the tests for the legacy module we removed last week.
Show me the coverage numbers from the last CI run.
